summary: Modern language models (LMs) are increasingly deployed with access to search tools at inference. Yet pretraining remains predominantly focused on predicting static text, with search capabilities typically introduced during post-training.
takeaways: Crucially, their advantage persists after supervised fine-tuning of both search-pretrained and conventionally pretrained models, indicating that the tested post-training procedures do not fully recover the capabilities developed during pretraining.
Yet pretraining remains predominantly focused on predicting static text, with search capabilities typically introduced during post-training.
We propose Search-Native Pretraining as a practical route to teach search capability during pretraining from ordinary text corpora.
